questionsToConsider: What do you always end up chasing a new client for in the first week? Ask for it here.
Do you need logins to the client's tools, and how will you collect them safely outside the form?
Who on your side reads the answers before kickoff, and how soon after the form comes in?
Should the priority ranking use your own trade-offs, such as scope, speed or budget?
guide.howToUseResponses: Read each response before the kickoff call and turn the success answer into the goal you write at the top of the project brief. Set your update rhythm and channel to match what the client chose, and put everyone named as an approver on the review list from day one. If the client said nothing is ready yet, send them a short checklist of what you need and by when.
customizeSteps: Swap the ranking items for the trade-offs that come up in your kind of project.
Edit the materials list so it names the files and access you actually need to start.
Send the link right after the contract is signed, so answers arrive before your kickoff call.

faqs.q: What should a client onboarding form include?
faqs.a: Contact details, a short project summary, what success looks like, deadlines, who signs off, how the client wants updates, and the files you need to start. Anything you would otherwise chase by email belongs here.

faqs.q: When should I send a client onboarding form?
faqs.a: Straight after the contract or proposal is signed and before the kickoff meeting. That way the meeting is spent on the plan rather than on collecting basics.

faqs.q: Should I collect passwords in an onboarding form?
faqs.a: No. Ask which tools you'll need access to, then have the client invite you or share access through a password manager.

faqs.q: Can I change the questions for different kinds of clients?
faqs.a: Yes. Use this template copies it into your account, where you can edit every question and branch, or make one copy per service you offer.

doc.title: Client onboarding
doc.description: Everything you need from a new client before kickoff, asked in the order a good project lead would.

blocks.title: Welcome aboard! A few questions now will save us a lot of back and forth later.
Who will be our main point of contact?
What's your company or brand called?
Your website, if you have one
In a few sentences, what are we working on together?
Three months from now, what would make this project a clear win for you?
blocks.description: A number, a launch, a feeling. Whatever you'd point to.

blocks.title: Put these in order of what matters most on this project
Is there a date this has to be ready by?
blocks.description: Skip this if there's no fixed date.

blocks.title: Who signs off on the work?
Who else needs to approve things, and how do they like to review?
blocks.description: Names and roles are enough. Tell us if anyone only wants to see the final version.

blocks.title: How do you prefer to hear from us?
How often would you like a progress update?
Which of these can you share with us now?

options.label: Logins or access to tools we'll need

blocks.title: Upload whatever is ready
blocks.description: Please don't upload passwords. We'll arrange access to accounts separately.

blocks.title: What's the first thing you need from us?
Has anything gone wrong with a past agency or supplier that we should make sure to avoid?

endings.title: You're all set 🙌
endings.bodyMd: Thanks! We'll read this before our kickoff call and come with a plan for the first two weeks.
